acorn's parser (acorn/src/expression.js) reports two errors in an object literal only once it knows the literal is not a destructuring pattern: a shorthand property with a default, as in {a = 0}, is "Shorthand property assignments are valid only in destructuring patterns", and a second __proto__ property is "Redefinition of __proto__ property". Today both errors are lost when the object literal is the object of a member expression that is itself an assignment target, although such a literal is never a pattern: with { ecmaVersion: 2022 }, parse("({a = 0}.x = 0);") succeeds, and so do parse("[{a = 0}.x] = [];"), parse("for ({a = 0}.x of []) ;") and parse("({__proto__: 1, __proto__: 2}.x = 0);"). Each must throw a SyntaxError: "({a = 0}.x = 0);" and "[{a = 0}.x] = [];" with "Shorthand property assignments are valid only in destructuring patterns (1:4)", "for ({a = 0}.x of []) ;" with the same message at (1:8), and "({__proto__: 1, __proto__: 2}.x = 0);" with "Redefinition of __proto__ property (1:16)". The same holds wherever such a literal is the object of a member expression that is assigned to or destructured into, however deep. What must not change: real destructuring patterns still parse ("({a = 0} = {});", "[{a = 0}] = [];", "({a = 0}) => 0;"), a member expression whose object has no such property still parses as a target ("[{a: 0}.x] = [];"), and the errors acorn reports today stay as they are ("({a = 0});" throws the shorthand message at (1:4); "({a = 0} += 1);" throws "Assigning to rvalue (1:1)"). The parser's source is in acorn/src; npm test builds it and runs the test files under test/ (the parser's expression tests are in test/tests-harmony.js, written with test() and testFail()). Add regression tests for this behaviour to the project's existing test suite. The project's tests run with npm test.
